claims.statement: Quietly confident of prospects for FY2025, focusing on diverse components and market share
Full-year EBITDA margin target of ~14% for FY25, already achieved in Q4 FY24
FY25 capex estimated at Rs 150 crore, mainly for JLR e-Axle and PSA capacity, automation, and maintenance
Capex of Rs 250-300 crore over next 3 years to support Rs 700-800 crore incremental revenue
New orders of Rs 150 crore booked in Q4 FY24; total order book Rs 9,150 crore executable over 6 years (FY24-FY29)
FY25 new business order booking target of Rs 1,200 crore; 83% from 4-wheelers, 56% from global customers, 22% non-auto, >8% hybrid
Normalised gross margin expected to settle in 50-52% range for FY25
Optimistic about FY25 prospects, strong pipeline of new business
Revenue target of ₹1,800 crore for FY25, representing ~15% growth; will update in Q2
Capex target of roughly ₹151 crore for FY25
Expect CAGR of approximately 15% to 16% in top line beyond FY26
New orders of ₹650 crore booked in Q1 FY25; total new order bookings since FY24 exceed ₹9,500 crore executable over 6 years
Global automotive customer awarded order for two critical parts produced in India for USA supply; potential life-of-order size over ₹500 crore
Gross margin 50.42% in Q1 FY25, up ~25 bps YoY due to improved product mix
Cold core box manufacturing facility added at Shikrapur Plant in Pune for structural parts; enables swing arm opportunities in India
FY25 revenue guidance of Rs 1,800 crore maintained but softening demand in India, Europe, USA may impact; update expected in Q3
FY26 revenue guidance not given due to market softness and lack of OEM volume clarity; will update next quarter
Medium-term target of 15% EBITDA margin and 20% ROCE remains on track despite short-term softness
FY25 capex guided at Rs 150 crore; H1 capex Rs 100 crore; FY26 capex expected Rs 90-100 crore
FY26 capex expectation between Rs 90 crore to Rs 100 crore for new business capacities
Q2 gross margin 47.55%, down 253 bps YoY due to mix shift (lower CV, higher 2W); EBITDA margin 12.2% vs 12.3% YoY
H1 gross margin 48.8% vs 50.2% YoY; EBITDA Rs 115 crore, up 32% YoY; PAT Rs 36 crore, up 49% YoY
European battery housing for Samsung (Tier 1) stabilized after Q1 ramp-up across 3 models; VW autonomous driving project progressing
Toyota TNGA line capacity expansion from Jan 2025; in-house modification in Nov 2024 with brief shutdown; higher volumes from Q4
Company believes nearing bottom of global industrial cycle slowdown
Strategic focus on product diversification, expanding market reach, strengthening leadership
FY26 revenue target of Rs 2,200 crore deferred by at least one year to FY27
Q3 FY25 gross margin fell 543 bps YoY to 45.81% due to adverse mix and new plant fixed costs
Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin dropped to 9% from 13% YoY; management expects sequential recovery
Upfront costs for new EV projects and automation ~Rs 4-5 crore in Q3; expected to decline in Q4
Q3 FY25 capex Rs 42 crore; 9M FY25 capex ~Rs 140 crore; Q4 FY25 capex expected Rs 20-25 crore
EV parts development capex to add Rs 250-300 crore capacity over next two years
Order book stands at Rs 9,000 crore as of today; Q3 added 7 parts worth ~Rs 500 crore
Order book covers next 5 years till FY29 based on current run-rate
Q3 FY25 average capacity utilisation 70-75%; new plants in ramp-up phase
In Q4 FY25, the Company has booked 1 new part from 1 customer
Revenue guidance for FY26 revised to Rs 1,900-1,950 crore, implying 12-14% growth
EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 around 13%
Order book Rs 9,000 crore executable through FY29, 82% four-wheeler (50% PV, 32% CV)
Capacity utilization ~75% in Q4 FY25, targeting ~80% in FY26 and FY27
Booked 7 new parts from 5 customers in Q1 FY26
Committed to building a future-ready organization resilient, diversified, and poised to capture emerging opportunities
Gross margin 45.9% in Q1 FY26, down 165 bps YoY from 47.5% due to aluminum price increase and export volume dip
EBITDA Rs 50 crore at 11.9% margin in Q1 FY26, up from Rs 48 crore and 11.2% in Q4 FY25, second consecutive quarter of margin improvement
Deployed Rs 30 crore capex in Q1 FY26, full year target intact at Rs 165-170 crore
Healthy order book of Rs 9,100 crore spanning FY23 to FY29, added Rs 1,600 crore last year, net after EV program reductions
Order book composition: 51% PV, 30% CV, 12% two-wheeler, 4% non-auto; geography split 48% domestic, 52% export
European OEM ramp-up: currently 150 sets/week, targeting 600 sets/week from January 2026
Export margins higher than domestic; non-auto more profitable but lower volumes; PV and CV have good margins
Previous revenue target of Rs 1,900 crore with 13-13.5% margin for FY26 likely to change due to headwinds; will reassess once tariff situation settles
No change in capex plan despite headwinds; committed to Rs 170 crore for FY26 and Rs 320 crore over two years
Cost reduction initiatives from last 3-4 quarters starting to show results in manufacturing costs; expected to be key lever for margins this year
Domestic auto demand expected to improve post GST rate rationalization
Global headwinds: macro volatility, tariff uncertainty, rare earth and semiconductor shortages, muted demand
Gross margin improved 300 bps QoQ to 48.9% driven by better product mix and operational efficiency
EBITDA margin rose 100 bps QoQ to 12.9%
Capex for Q2 was Rs. 32 crore; H1 total Rs. 63 crore; full-year guidance Rs. 125-130 crore
Order book stands at Rs. 9,100 crore executable FY24-FY29; Rs. 650-700 crore already consumed
Seven new parts won from six customers in Q2 with 5-year potential revenue of Rs. 257 crore
All current plants full; new location being evaluated at Khed City land bank for capacity expansion
Next year capex estimated Rs. 130-140 crore; Rs. 25-30 crore maintenance, Rs. 20-25 crore technology/automation, balance for capacity
Management expects double-digit top-line growth in FY27 but will give clearer picture in Q4 FY26
EBITDA margins expected to improve further in Q3 and Q4 FY26 over Q2
Optimistic for Q4 FY26 and next fiscal year, focused on strategic initiatives
Expects domestic revenue to improve 10-12% sequentially in Q4 FY26 without global exposure.
Targets EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% in Q4 FY26 and 12-12.5% for full year FY26; aims to reach 13% and then 14% EBITDA margin over time.
Order book of approximately Rs. 9,100 crore to be executed by FY29; Rs. 850-900 crore utilized so far; exit revenue target of ~Rs. 3,500 crore by FY29.
Secured 4 new part orders in Q3 FY26: 3 ICE, 1 carbon-neutral; 3 domestic, 1 global (German OEM eAxle housing); 3 CV, 1 PV segment.
Gross margin improved 138 bps YoY to 47.2% in Q3 FY26 on favorable mix and operating leverage; declined 170 bps QoQ from 48.9% due to mix changes and input cost volatility.
EBITDA grew 34% YoY to Rs. 47.2 crore in Q3 FY26; EBITDA margin 10.9% vs 12.9% in Q2 FY26 due to higher employee costs, translation costs, and asset write-offs.
Capex of Rs. 28 crore in Q3 FY26; cumulative 9M FY26 capex Rs. 92 crore; on track for full year FY26 capex of Rs. 125-130 crore focused on automation, capacity enhancement, and new program readiness.

Plants operating at ~75% utilization; cannot directly correlate utilization increase to revenue growth due to need for new machines for complex/bigger parts; existing facilities can generate Rs. 200 crore with old systems.
Capital expenditure on property plant and equipment and intangible assets (Consolidated) Rs 131.99 crore
Capital expenditure on intangible assets (Consolidated) Rs 15.38 crore
FY26 Capex Rs 1,473.6 mn (Rs 147.4 cr)
Board recommended dividend of Rs 2 per share (face value Rs 5) for FY26
Confident of building momentum in FY27; priorities: value addition, product diversification, technology enhancement, increasing share of wallet
FY27 revenue growth target of 8-10% excluding aluminum price impact
FY27 EBITDA expected to grow ~20% with margin improvement of ~1.5 percentage points
claims.value: 20% plus we are expecting increase in the EBITDA margins

FY27 capex plan of approximately Rs 150 crore

Entry into two large Indian PV and CV OEMs with Rs 850 crore visibility over five years

Expects 1% margin improvement in FY27 over FY26 adjusted margin of 11.4%

Further investments beyond Rs 125 crore Pune plant confirmed; more capacity additions planned

Investment in the new facility in Pune is being phased in line with secured customer programs, with production targeted to commence by April 2027
Focus for second half is on disciplined execution, improving operational efficiency and translating growing business scale into stronger margins

Targets 14-15% EBITDA margin by FY30

~30 new part numbers expected to start production in next 1 year

100% of raw material price inflation passed through to customers
